nodes.description: Autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2K (LGMD2K) is a form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy characterized by the onset of slowly progressive proximal muscle weakness during childhood (with fatigue and difficulty running and climbing stairs) and developmental delay. Mild intellectual deficit and microcephaly, without any obvious structural brain abnormality, are found in all pat

nodes.name: muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy (congenital with intellectual disability), type B1
qualitative or quantitative defects of protein O-mannosyltransferase 1
autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss 7
nodes.description: Any autosomal recessive nonsyndromic deafness in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TMC1 gene.

nodes.name: autosomal dominant nonsyndromic hearing loss 36
nodes.description: Any autosomal dominant nonsyndromic deafness in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TMC1 gene.

nodes.name: metatropic dysplasia
nodes.description: Metatropic dysplasia (MTD) is a rare spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia characterized by a long trunk and short limbs in infancy followed by severe and progressive kyphoscoliosis causing a reversal in proportions during childhood (short trunk and long limbs) and a final short stature in adulthood.

nodes.name: parastremmatic dwarfism
nodes.description: Parastremmatic dwarfism is a very rare chondrodysplasia characterized by severe dwarfism, kyphoscoliosis, stiffness of large joints and distortion of lower limbs.

nodes.name: spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia, Maroteaux type
nodes.description: A very rare type of spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia described in fewer than 10 patients to date and characterized clinically by dysplastic epiphyses, short stature appearing in infancy, short neck, short and stubby hands and feet, scoliosis, genu valgum, abnormal pelvis, osteoporosis and osteoarthritis.

nodes.name: spondylometaphyseal dysplasia, Kozlowski type
nodes.description: Spondylometaphyseal dysplasia, Kozlowski type is characterized by short stature (short-trunk dwarfism), scoliosis, metaphyseal abnormalities in the femur (prominent in the femoral neck and trochanteric area), coxa vara and generalized platyspondyly.

nodes.name: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease axonal type 2C
nodes.description: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2C (CMT2C) is a form of axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, a peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy, characterized by the association of vocal cord anomalies, impairment of respiratory muscles and sensorineural hearing loss with the distal hands and feet weakness. Onset is between infancy and the 6th decade.

nodes.name: familial digital arthropathy-brachydactyly
nodes.description: Familial digital arthropathy-brachydactyly is characterized by the association of arthropathy of interphalangeal, metacarpophalangeal and metatarsophalangeal joints with brachydactyly of the middle and distal phalanges. It has been described in numerous members from five generations of one large family. Inheritance is autosomal dominant.

nodes.name: brachyolmia
nodes.description: Brachyolmia is a rare, clinically and genetically heterogeneous group of bone disorders characterized by short trunk, mild short stature, scoliosis and generalized platyspondyly without significant abnormalities in the long bones.

nodes.name: avascular necrosis of femoral head, primary, 2
autosomal dominant brachyolmia
nodes.description: Autosomal dominant brachyolmia is a relatively severe form of brachyolmia, a group of rare genetic skeletal disorders, characterized by short-trunked short stature, platyspondyly and kyphoscoliosis. Degenerative joint disease (osteoarthropathy) in the spine, large joints and interphalangeal joints becomes manifest in adulthood.

nodes.name: scapuloperoneal spinal muscular atrophy, autosomal dominant
neuronopathy, distal hereditary motor, autosomal dominant 8
nodes.description: Autosomal dominant congenital benign spinal muscular atrophy is a rare distal hereditary motor neuropathy, with a variable clinical phenotype, typically characterized by congenital, non-progressive, predominantly distal, lower limb muscle weakness and atrophy and congenital (or early-onset) flexion contractures of the hip, knee and ankle joints. Reduced or absent lower limb deep tendon reflexes, s

nodes.name: inborn aminoacylase deficiency
nodes.description: An inherited metabolic disease that is has its basis in the disruption of aminoacylase activity.

nodes.name: SLC26A2-related skeletal dysplasia
nodes.description: Any skeletal disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variant in the SLC26A2 gene. This includes SLC26A2-related achondrogenesis, SLC26A2-related atelosteogenesis, SLC26A2-related diastrophic dysplasia, and SLC26A2-related multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.

nodes.name: diastrophic dysplasia
nodes.description: Diastrophic dwarfism is a rare disorder marked by short stature with short extremities (final adult height is 120cm +/- 10cm), and joint malformations leading to multiple joint contractures (principally involving the shoulders, elbows, interphalangeal joints and hips).

nodes.name: multiple epiphyseal dysplasia type 4
nodes.description: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia type 4 is a multiple epiphyseal dysplasia with a late-childhood onset, characterized by joint pain involving hips, knees, wrists, and fingers with occasional limitation of joint movements, deformity of hands, feet, and knees (club foot, clinodactyly, brachydactyly), scoliosis and slightly reduced adult height. Radiographs display flat epiphyses with early arthritis of

nodes.name: achondrogenesis type IB
nodes.description: Achondrogenesis type 1B (ACG1B), a form of achondrogenesis, is a rare lethal skeletal dysplasia characterized by severe micromelia with very short fingers and toes, a flat face, a short neck, thickened soft tissue around the neck, hypoplasia of the thorax, protuberant abdomen, a hydropic fetal appearance and distinctive histological features of the cartilage.

nodes.name: atelosteogenesis type II
nodes.description: A lethal perinatal bone dysplasia characterized by limb shortening, normal sized skull with cleft palate, hitchhiker thumbs, distinctive facial dysmorphism and radiographic skeletal features, caused by mutations in the diastrophic dysplasia sulfate transporter gene.

nodes.name: glaucoma 3A
nodes.description: An autosomal recessive form of congenital glaucoma caused by mutation(s) in the CYP1B1 gene, encoding cytochrome P450 1B1.

nodes.name: CYP1B1-related glaucoma with or without anterior segment dysgenesis
nodes.description: Any primary congenital glaucoma in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the CYP1B1 gene.

nodes.name: congenital glaucoma
nodes.description: A developmental glaucoma that results from the abnormal development of the aqueous drainage structure, characterized by an elevated intra-ocular pressure, enlargement of globe (buphthalmos), corneal edema and optic nerve cupping, and presenting clinically with the characteristic triad of epiphora, photophobia and blepharospasm.

nodes.name: TEK-related primary glaucoma
nodes.description: Any primary hereditary glaucoma in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TEK gene.

nodes.name: multiple cutaneous and mucosal venous malformations
nodes.description: Mucocutaneous venous malformations (VMCMs) are hereditary vascular malformations characterized by the presence of small, multifocal, bluish-purple venous lesions involving the skin and mucosa.

nodes.name: primary congenital glaucoma
nodes.description: Primary congenital glaucoma (PCG) is characterized by elevated intraocular pressure (IOP), enlargement of the globe (buphthalmos), edema, and opacification of the cornea with rupture of Descemet's membrane (Haab's striae), thinning of the anterior sclera and iris atrophy, anomalously deep anterior chamber, and structurally normal posterior segment except for progressive glaucomatous optic atrophy.

nodes.name: microspherophakia and/or megalocornea, with ectopia lentis and with or without secondary glaucoma
Weill-Marchesani syndrome 3
nodes.description: Any Weill-Marchesani syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the LTBP2 gene.

nodes.name: Weill-Marchesani syndrome
nodes.description: Weill-Marchesani syndrome (WMS) is a rare condition characterized by short stature, brachydactyly, joint stiffness, and characteristic eye abnormalities including microspherophakia, ectopia of the lens, severe myopia, and glaucoma.

nodes.name: LTBP2-related ocular dysgenesis
nodes.description: Any ocular dysgenesis disorder in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the LTBP2 gene.

nodes.name: early-infantile DEE
nodes.description: A neonatal/infantile epilepsy syndrome characterized by frequent drug-resistant seizures that begin ≤3 months of age, with abnormal interictal EEG and neurological examination. In up to 80% of patients, EIDEE is caused by an underlying structural, genetic, or metabolic reason.

nodes.name: orofacial cleft
nodes.description: A disorder of facial skeleton that is characterized by cleft lip and/or cleft palate that result in feeding, speech and hearing problems caused by failures during development.

nodes.name: ADULT syndrome
nodes.description: ADULT (Acro-dermo-ungual-lacrimal-tooth) syndrome is a rare ectodermal dysplasia syndrome characterized by ectrodactyly, syndactyly, mammary hypoplasia, and excessive freckling as well as other typical ectodermal defects such as hypodontia, lacrimal duct anomalies, hypotrichosis, and onychodysplasia.

nodes.name: ankyloblepharon-ectodermal defects-cleft lip/palate syndrome
nodes.description: An ectodermal dysplasia syndrome with defining features of ankyloblepharon filiforme adnatum (AFA), ectodermal abnormalities and a cleft lip and/or palate.

nodes.name: EEC syndrome
nodes.description: EEC syndrome is a genetic developmental disorder characterized by ectrodactyly, ectodermal dysplasia, and orofacial clefts (cleft lip/palate).

nodes.name: limb-mammary syndrome
nodes.description: Limb-mammary syndrome (LMS) is a rare disease belonging to the group of ectodermal dysplasias.

nodes.name: ectrodactyly, ectodermal dysplasia, and cleft lip-palate syndrome 3
nodes.description: Any EEC syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TP63 gene.

nodes.name: split hand-foot malformation 4
nodes.description: Any split hand-foot malformation in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TP63 gene.

nodes.name: TP63-related ectodermal dysplasia spectrum with limb and orofacial malformations
nodes.description: Any developmental defect during embryogenesis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TP63 gene. This disease is characterized by variable ectodermal dysplasia, limb defects, and orofacial clefting.

nodes.name: cleft lip
nodes.description: A congenital abnormality consisting of one or more clefts (splits) in the upper lip, which may be accompanied by a cleft palate; it is the result of the failure of the embryonic parts of the lip to fuse.

nodes.name: Rapp-Hodgkin syndrome
nodes.description: A form of ectodermal dysplasia characterized by the association of anhidrotic ectodermal dysplasia with cleft lip/palate.

nodes.name: achondrogenesis type IA
nodes.description: Achondrogenesis type 1A (ACG1A), a form of achondrogenesis, is a very rare, lethal skeletal dysplasia characterized by dwarfism with extremely short limbs, narrow chest, short ribs that are easily fractured, soft skull bones and distinctive histological features of the cartilage.

nodes.name: odontochondrodysplasia 1
nodes.description: A very rare syndrome associating chondrodysplasia with dentinogenesis imperfecta.

nodes.name: TRIP11-related skeletal dysplasia
nodes.description: Any skeletal dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the TRIP11 gene. Reduced protein function in TRIP11 causes a spectrum of skeletal symptoms from a more mild phenotype, called ondontochondrodysplasia, with features including short stature and joint laxity to a more severe phenotype, called achondrogenesis type 1A, which presents as a lethal prenatal or neonatal skeletal dy

nodes.name: cataract 41
nodes.description: Any early-onset non-syndromic cataract in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the WFS1 gene.

nodes.name: Wolfram syndrome 1
nodes.description: Any Wolfram syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the WFS1 gene.

nodes.name: autosomal dominant nonsyndromic hearing loss 6
nodes.description: Any autosomal dominant nonsyndromic deafness in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the WFS1 gene.

nodes.name: Wolfram syndrome
nodes.description: Wolfram syndrome (WS) also known as DIDMOAD, is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by type I diabetes mellitus (DM), diabetes insipidus (DI), sensorineural deafness (D), bilateral optical atrophy (OA) and neurological signs. Other related problems are urinary tract atony, ataxia, peripheral neuropathy, psychiatric disorders and/or seizures. 2 types of WS may be distinguished: type 1 and ty

nodes.name: Wolfram-like syndrome
nodes.description: Wolfram-like syndrome is a rare endocrine disease characterized by the triad of adult-onset diabetes mellitus, progressive hearing loss (usually presenting in the first decade of life and principally of low to moderate frequencies), and/or juvenile-onset optic atrophy. Psychiatric (i.e. anxiety, depression, hallucinations) and sleep disorders, the only neurologic abnormalities observed in this dis

nodes.name: nephrogenic syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis
nodes.description: Nephrogenic syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis (NSIAD) is a rare genetic disorder of water balance, closely resembling the far more frequent syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic secretion (SIAD), and characterized by euvolemic hypotonic hyponatremia due to impaired free water excretion and undetectable or low plasma arginine vasopressin (AVP) levels.

nodes.name: nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
nodes.description: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (NDI) is characterized by polyuria with polydipsia, recurrent bouts of fever, constipation, and acute hypernatremic dehydration after birth that may cause neurological sequelae. Polyuria may exceed 10 liters in children.

nodes.name: epiphyseal dysplasia, multiple, 3
nodes.description: Any multiple epiphyseal dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the COL9A3 gene.

nodes.name: multiple epiphyseal dysplasia due to collagen 9 anomaly
nodes.description: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia due to collagen 9 anomaly is a rare primary bone dysplasia disorder characterized by normal or mild short stature, early-onset pain and/or stiffness of the joints (mainly affecting knees but also elbows, wrists, ankles and fingers, with relative sparing of the hips) and early degenerative joint disease. Other skeletal anomalies (incl. varus or valgus deformities, oste

nodes.name: Darier disease
nodes.description: Darier disease (DD) is a keratinization disorder characterized by the development of keratotic papules in seborrheic areas and specific nail anomalies.

nodes.name: acrokeratosis verruciformis
nodes.description: A rare genetic skin keratinization disorder with an autosomal dominant mode of inheritance. It is characterized by numerous flesh-colored warty papules on the back of the hands, medial aspect of the feet, knees, and elbows.

nodes.name: brachydactyly type B1
nodes.description: Any brachydactyly type B in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ROR2 gene.

nodes.name: brachydactyly type B
nodes.description: A condition characterized by incomplete development (hypoplasia) or absence of the outermost bones of the fingers and toes (distal phalanges) and nails. Additional features may include hypoplasia of the middle phalanges, fusion of the joints (symphalangism), broad thumbs, and webbed fingers (syndactyly). The feet are often less severely affected than the hands. There are 2 types of this condition,

nodes.name: Robinow syndrome
nodes.description: Robinow syndrome (RS) is a rare genetic syndrome characterized by limb shortening and abnormalities of the head, face and external genitalia.

nodes.name: autosomal recessive Robinow syndrome
nodes.description: Autosomal recessive Robinow syndrome (RRS) is the less common type of Robinow syndrome (RS) characterized by short-limb dwarfism, costovertebral segmentation defects and abnormalities of the head, face and external genitalia.

nodes.name: mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome 8a
nodes.description: Any mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the RRM2B gene.

nodes.name: progressive external ophthalmoplegia with mitochondrial DNA deletions, autosomal dominant 5
nodes.description: Any progressive external ophthalmoplegia with mitochondrial DNA deletions in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the RRM2B gene.

nodes.name: mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome, encephalomyopathic form
nodes.description: Mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome, encephalomyopathic form is a group of mitochondrial DNA maintenance syndrome diseases characterized by predominantly neuromuscular manifestations with typically infantile onset of hypotonia, lactic acidosis, psychomotor delay, progressive hyperkinetic-dystonic movement disorders, external ophtalmoplegia, sensosineural hearing loss, generalized seizures and var

nodes.name: rod-cone dystrophy, sensorineural deafness, and Fanconi-type renal dysfunction
mitochondrial neurogastrointestinal encephalomyopathy
nodes.description: A syndrome characterized by the association of gastrointestinal dysmotility, peripheral neuropathy, chronic progressive external ophthalmoplegia and leukoencephalopathy.

nodes.name: retinitis pigmentosa 35
nodes.description: Any retinitis pigmentosa in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the SEMA4A gene.

nodes.name: cone-rod dystrophy 10
nodes.description: Any cone-rod dystrophy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the SEMA4A gene.

nodes.name: Juberg-Hayward syndrome
nodes.description: Juberg-Hayward syndrome is a polymalformative syndrome that associates multiple skeletal anomalies with microcephaly, facial dysmorphism, urogenital anomalies and intellectual deficit.

nodes.name: Roberts-SC phocomelia syndrome
nodes.description: A rare genetic syndrome with an autosomal recessive pattern of inheritance. It is caused by a mutation in the ESCO2 gene. Clinical signs at birth include multiple limb and facial abnormalities.

nodes.name: striatonigral degeneration
nodes.description: A progressive neurodegenerative disorder caused by a disruption in the connection between the striatum and the substantia nigra. It is a type of multiple system atrophy (MSA). Signs and symptoms include rigidity, instability, impaired speech, and slow movements.

nodes.name: infantile bilateral striatal necrosis
nodes.description: Several syndromes of bilateral symmetric spongy degeneration of the caudate nucleaus, putamen and globus pallidus characterized by developmental regression, choreoathetosis and dystonia progressing to spastic quadriparesis. IBSN can be familial or sporadic.

nodes.name: inherited blood coagulation disorder
nodes.description: Hemorrhagic and thrombotic disorders that occur as a consequence of inherited abnormalities in blood coagulation.

nodes.name: torsion dystonia 4
nodes.description: DYT4 type primary dystonia is characterized by predominantly laryngeal dystonia (manifesting as whispering dysphonia) and cervical dystonia (manifesting as torticollis).

nodes.name: leukodystrophy, hypomyelinating, 6
nodes.description: A leukodystrophy characterized by slowly progressive spasticity, extrapyramidal movement disorders (dystonia, choreoathetosis and rigidity), cerebellar ataxia, moderate to severe cognitive deficit, and anarthria/dysarthria.

nodes.name: TUBB4A-related neurologic disorder
nodes.description: Any neurologic condition in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TUBB4A gene.

nodes.name: focal, segmental or multifocal dystonia
nodes.description: A rare neurologic movement disorder characterized by sustained muscle contractions of a single body region, usually producing twisting and repetitive movements or abnormal postures or positions.

nodes.name: early-onset generalized limb-onset dystonia
nodes.description: A rare movement disorder characterized by involuntary, repetitive, sustained muscle contractions or postures involving one or more sites of the body.

nodes.name: early-onset generalized dystonia
nodes.description: A generalized isolated dystonia characterized by early-onset, which may be clinically indistinguishable from DYT-TOR1A and may be the most common cause of early-onset generalized dystonia, at least outside the Askenazi Jewish population.

nodes.name: maple syrup urine disease
nodes.description: An autosomal recessive inherited disorder caused by mutations in the BCKDHA, BCKDHB, DBT, and DLD genes. It is characterized by a deficiency of branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex, leading to accumulation of metabolites in the body fluids. The name of the disease derives from the sweet odor of the urine in infants, reminiscent of maple syrup. Signs and symptoms usually appear in i

nodes.name: inherited lipoic acid biosynthesis defect
nodes.description: An inherited metabolic disease that is has its basis in the disruption of lipoate biosynthetic process.

nodes.name: pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency
nodes.description: A rare neurometabolic disorder characterized by a wide range of clinical signs with metabolic and neurological components of varying severity. Manifestations range from often fatal, severe, neonatal lactic acidosis to later-onset neurological disorders. Six subtypes related to the affected subunit of the PDH complex have been recognized with significant clinical overlap: PDHD due to E1-alpha, E1-b

nodes.name: choreatic disease
nodes.description: A neurological condition affecting the involuntary movements. It is characterized by brief, non-repetitive irregular muscle contractions. It is seen in patients with Huntington's disease.

nodes.name: brain-lung-thyroid syndrome
nodes.description: Brain-lung-thyroid syndrome is a rare disorder characterized by congenital hypothyroidism (CH), infant respiratory distress syndrome (IRDS) and benign hereditary chorea (BHC).

nodes.name: NKX2-1 related choreoathetosis and congenital hypothyroidism with or without pulmonary dysfunction
nodes.description: The NKX2-1 gene is located on chromosome 14 at 14q13.3 and encodes the NK2 homeobox 1 protein, a transcription factor that binds and activates thyroid specific genes. NKX2-1 was first reported in relation to autosomal dominant NKX2-1 related choreoathetosis and congenital hypothyroidism with or without pulmonary dysfunction in 1998.

nodes.name: autosomal dominant mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial diseases due to partial IFNgammaR1 deficiency
nodes.description: A genetic variant of Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease characterized by a partial deficiency leading to impaired IFN-gamma immunity and, consequently, recurrent, moderately severe infections with bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) and other environmental mycobacteria (EM).

nodes.name: thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
nodes.description: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) is an aggressive and life-threatening form of thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) characterized by profound peripheral thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (MAHA) and organ failure of variable severity and is comprised of congenital TTP and acquired TTP.

nodes.name: fibromatosis
nodes.description: A poorly circumscribed neoplasm arising from the soft tissues. It is characterized by the presence of spindle-shaped fibroblasts and an infiltrative growth pattern.

nodes.name: soft tissue neoplasm
nodes.description: A benign, intermediate, or malignant neoplasm that arises from the soft tissue. The most common types are lipomatous (fatty), vascular, smooth muscle, fibrous, and fibrohistiocytic neoplasms.

nodes.name: desmoid tumor
nodes.description: A desmoid tumor (DT) is a benign, locally invasive soft tissue tumor associated with a high recurrence rate but with no metastatic potential.

nodes.name: hereditary gastric cancer
nodes.description: Hereditary gastric cancer refers to the occurrence of gastric cancer in a familial context and is described as two or more cases of gastric cancer in first or second degree relatives with at least one case diagnosed before the age of 50. Familial clustering is observed in 10% of all cases of gastric cancer, and includes hereditary diffuse gastric cancer (early onset diffuse-type gastric cancer), g

nodes.name: familial adenomatous polyposis 1
nodes.description: An autosomal dominant disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the APC gene, characterized by the development of colorectal adenomatous polyposis, a very high risk of colorectal cancer and other extracolonic manifestations including both classic and attenuated familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP).

nodes.name: gastric adenocarcinoma and proximal polyposis of the stomach
nodes.description: An autosomal dominant disorder caused by specific pathogenic variants in the APC gene promoter, characterized by proximal gastric polyposis and an increased risk of gastric adenocarcinoma.

nodes.name: arthrogryposis, cleft palate, craniosynostosis, and impaired intellectual development
parkinsonism-dystonia, infantile
nodes.description: Infantile dystonia-parkinsonism (IPD) is an extremely rare inherited neurological syndrome that presents in early infancy with hypokinetic parkinsonism and dystonia and that can be fatal.

nodes.name: neurodevelopmental disorder, mitochondrial, with abnormal movements and lactic acidosis, with or without seizures
Desbuquois dysplasia 1
nodes.description: Any Desbuquois dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the CANT1 gene.

nodes.name: Desbuquois dysplasia
nodes.description: Desbuquois syndrome (DBQD) is an osteochondrodysplasia characterized by severe micromelic dwarfism, facial dysmorphism, joint laxity with multiple dislocations, vertebral and metaphyseal abnormalities and advanced carpotarsal ossification. Two forms have been distinguished on the basis of the presence (type 1) or the absence (type 2) of characteristic hand anomalies. A variant form of DBQD, Kim va

nodes.name: multiple mitochondrial dysfunctions syndrome 9b
nodes.description: A mitochondrial dysfunction syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the FDXR gene. It is characterized by optic atrophy and/or auditory neuropathy variably associated with developmental delay or regression, global hypotonia, pyramidal and cerebellar signs, and seizures.

nodes.name: FDXR-related optic atrophy mitochondrial dysfunction syndrome
nodes.description: Any mitochondrial disorder in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the FDXR gene.

nodes.name: auditory neuropathy-optic atrophy syndrome
nodes.description: A mitochondrial dysfunction syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the FDXR gene. It is characterized by onset of visual and hearing impairment in the first or second decades.

nodes.name: neurodevelopmental disorder with microcephaly and speech delay, with or without brain abnormalities
cutis laxa, autosomal dominant 1
nodes.description: Any autosomal dominant cutis laxa in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ELN gene.

nodes.name: supravalvular aortic stenosis
nodes.description: SupraValvar Aortic Stenosis (SVAS) is characterized by the narrowing of the aorta lumen (close to its origin) or other arteries (branch pulmonary arteries, coronary arteries). This narrowing of the aorta or pulmonary branches may impede blood flow, resulting in heart murmur and ventricular hypertrophy (in case of aorta involvement). The narrowing results from a thickening of the artery wall, which

nodes.name: partial deletion of the long arm of chromosome 7
nodes.description: Chromosome 7q deletion is a chromosome abnormality that occurs when there is a missing copy of the genetic material located on the long arm (q) of chromosome 7. The severity of the condition and the signs and symptoms depend on the size and location of the deletion and which genes are involved. Features that often occur in people with chromosome 7q deletion include developmental delay, intellectua

nodes.name: aortic valve stenosis
nodes.description: Aortic valve stenosis (AVS) is a condition characterized by narrowing of the heart's aortic valve opening. This narrowing prevents the valve from opening fully, which obstructs blood flow from the heart into the aorta, and onward to the rest of the body. AVS can range from mild to severe. Signs and symptoms typically develop when the narrowing of the opening is severe and may include chest pain (a

nodes.name: neurodevelopmental disorder
nodes.description: A behavioral and cognitive disorder with onset during the developmental period that involves impaired or aberrant development of intellectual, motor, or social functions.

nodes.name: Williams syndrome
nodes.description: A rare genetic multisystemic neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by a distinct facial appearance, cardiac anomalies (most frequently supravalvular aortic stenosis), cognitive and developmental abnormalities, and connective tissue abnormalities (such as joint laxity)

nodes.name: primary myelofibrosis
nodes.description: Myelofibrosis with myeloid metaplasia is a myeloproliferative disease with annual incidence of approximately 1 case per 100,000 individuals and age at diagnosis around 60 (an increased prevalence is noted in Ashkenazi Jews). nodes.name: thrombocythemia 2
nodes.description: Familial thrombocytosis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the MPL gene that produces constitutive activation of the thrombopoietin receptor, leading to excessive megakaryocyte proliferation and elevated platelet counts. nodes.name: acquired aplastic anemia
nodes.description: An instance of aplastic anemia that is acquired during the lifetime of the individual.

nodes.name: familial thrombocytosis
nodes.description: Familial thrombocytosis is a type of thrombocytosis, a sustained elevation of platelet numbers, which affects the platelet/megakaryocyte lineage and may create a tendency for thrombosis and hemorrhage but does not cause myeloproliferation.

nodes.name: congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia 1
nodes.description: Any congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the MPL gene. nodes.name: endocrine pancreas disorder
nodes.description: A disease involving the endocrine pancreas.

nodes.name: Donohue syndrome
nodes.description: Leprechaunism is a congenital form of extreme insulin resistance (a group of syndromes that also includes Rabson-Mensenhall syndrome, type A insulin-resistance syndrome, and acquired type B insulin-resistance syndrome) characterized by intrauterine and mainly postnatal severe growth retardation.

nodes.name: Rabson-Mendenhall syndrome
nodes.description: Rabson-Mendenhall syndrome belongs to the group of extreme insulin-resistance syndromes (which also includes leprechaunism, the lipodystrophies, and the type A and B insulin resistance syndromes).

nodes.name: hypertrichosis
nodes.description: Excessive hair growth anywhere on the body.

nodes.name: hyperinsulinism due to INSR deficiency
nodes.description: Hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia due to INSR deficiency is a very rare autosomal dominant form of familial hyperinsulinism characterized clinically in the single reported family by postprandial hypoglycemia, fasting hyperinsulinemia, and an elevated serum insulin-to-C peptide ratio, and a variable age of onset.

nodes.name: insulin-resistance syndrome type A
nodes.description: Type A insulin-resistance syndrome belongs to the group of extreme insulin-resistance syndromes (which includes leprechaunism, the lipodystrophies, Rabson-Mendenhall syndrome and type B insulin resistance syndrome) and is characterized by the triad of hyperinsulinemia, acanthosis nigricans (skin lesions associated with insulin resistance), and signs of hyperandrogenism in females without lipodystr

nodes.name: familial hyperinsulinism
nodes.description: An instance of hyperinsulinism (disease) that is caused by an inherited modification of the individual's genome.

nodes.name: partial deletion of the short arm of chromosome 16
Olmsted syndrome 1
nodes.description: Any Olmsted syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the TRPV3 gene.

nodes.name: glycogen storage disease due to acid maltase deficiency, infantile onset
nodes.description: Glycogen storage disease due to acid maltase deficiency, infantile onset is the most severe form of glycogen storage disease due to acid maltase deficiency, characterized by cardiomegaly with respiratory distress, muscle weakness and feeding difficulties. It is often fatal.

nodes.name: glycogen storage disease due to acid maltase deficiency, late-onset
nodes.description: Glycogen storage disease due to acid maltase deficiency, late onset (AMDL), a form of Glycogen storage disease due to acid maltase deficiency (AMD), a degenerative metabolic myopathy particularly affecting respiratory and skeletal muscles, is characterized by an accumulation of glycogen in lysosomes.

nodes.name: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 33
nodes.description: Any early infantile epileptic encephalopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the EEF1A2 gene.

nodes.name: autosomal dominant palmoplantar keratoderma and congenital alopecia
nodes.description: Autosomal dominant palmoplantar keratoderma with congenital alopecia (PPK-CA) is a rare genetic skin disorder characterized by absence of scalp and body hair and palmoplantar keratoderma, without other hand complications.

nodes.name: syndactyly type 3
nodes.description: Syndactyly type 3 (SD3) is a rare congenital distal limb malformation characterized by complete and bilateral syndactyly between the 4th and 5th fingers.

nodes.name: craniometaphyseal dysplasia, autosomal recessive
nodes.description: Autosomal recessive form of craniometaphyseal dysplasia.

nodes.name: craniometaphyseal dysplasia
nodes.description: Craniometaphyseal dysplasia (CMD) is a very rare genetic bone disease characterized by progressive diffuse hyperostosis of cranial bones causing facial dysmorphism and functional repercussions, and metaphyseal widening of long bones.

nodes.name: oculodentodigital dysplasia
nodes.description: Oculodentodigital dysplasia (ODDD) is characterized by craniofacial, neurologic, limb and ocular abnormalities.

nodes.name: oculodentodigital dysplasia, autosomal recessive
nodes.description: Autosomal recessive form of oculodentodigital dysplasia.

nodes.name: basal ganglia calcification, idiopathic, 6
nodes.description: Any bilateral striopallidodentate calcinosis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the XPR1 gene.

nodes.name: segmental dystonia
nodes.description: A dystonia that affects two or more adjacent parts of the body.

nodes.name: dystonia 27
nodes.description: Any dystonic disorder in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the COL6A3 gene.

nodes.name: hereditary spastic paraplegia 57
nodes.description: An extremely rare, complex type of hereditary spastic paraplegia, characterized by onset in infancy of pronounced leg spasticity (leading to the inability to walk independently), reduced visual acuity due to optic atrophy, and distal wasting of the hands and feet due to an axonal demyelinating sensorimotor neuropathy. nodes.name: hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy, Okinawa type
nodes.description: Hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy, Okinawa type is a rare, genetic, axonal hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy characterized by the adult-onset of slowly progressive, symmetric, proximal dominant muscle weakness and atrophy, painful muscle cramps, fasciculations and distal sensory impairment, mostly (but not exclusively) in individuals (and their descendents) from the Okinawa region in J

nodes.name: childhood-onset epilepsy syndrome with developmental and/or epileptic encephalopathy
nodes.description: A childhood-onset epilepsy syndrome where the onset of the condition includes manifestations of cognitive, neurological, or psychiatric impairment, stagnation, or regression, due directly to the underlying etiology. nodes.name: monilethrix
nodes.description: Monilethrix is a rare genodermatosis characterized by a hair shaft dysplasia resulting in hypotrichosis.

nodes.name: campomelic dysplasia
nodes.description: Campomelic dysplasia is a very rare disorder characterized by a variable association of skeletal abnormalities (bowed and fragile long bones, pelvis and chest abnormalities, eleven rib pairs instead of the usual twelve), and extraskeletal abnormalities (facial dysmorphology, cleft palate, sexual ambiguity or sex reversal in two thirds of the affected boys, and brain, heart and kidney malformations

nodes.name: nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome
nodes.description: A rare hereditary disorder due to autosomal dominant transmission with hamartosis characterized by multiple early-onset basal cell carcinoma (BCC), multiple jaw keratocysts and skeletal abnormalities.

nodes.name: cataract 40
nodes.description: Any early-onset non-syndromic cataract in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the NHS gene.

nodes.name: Nance-Horan syndrome
nodes.description: A syndrome characterized by the association in male patients of congenital cataracts with microcornea, dental anomalies and facial dysmorphism.

nodes.name: Larsen-like syndrome, B3GAT3 type
nodes.description: Larsen-like syndrome, B3GAT3 type is a rare, genetic, primary bone dysplasia characterized by laxity, dislocations and contractures of the joints, short stature, foot deformities (e.g. clubfeet), broad tips of fingers and toes, short neck, dysmorphic facial features (hypertelorism, downslanting palpebral fissures, upturned nose with anteverted nares, high arched palate) and various cardiac malform

nodes.name: spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia with congenital joint dislocations
nodes.description: CHST3-related skeletal dysplasia is a very rare bone disorder characterized clinically by short stature of prenatal onset; dislocation of the knees, hips or elbows; club feet; limitation of range of motion of large joints; progressive kyphosis; and occasional scoliosis. In a few patients, minor heart valve dysplasia has also been described. Intellect, vision and hearing are normal.

nodes.name: short-rib thoracic dysplasia 13 with or without polydactyly
nodes.description: An asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy that has material basis in homozygous mutation in the CEP120 gene on chromosome 5q23.

nodes.name: spastic ataxia 3
nodes.description: Any autosomal recessive spastic ataxia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the MARS2 gene.

nodes.name: combined oxidative phosphorylation defect type 25
nodes.description: Any combined oxidative phosphorylation deficiency in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the MARS2 gene.

nodes.name: centronuclear myopathy
nodes.description: Centronuclear myopathy (CNM) is an inherited neuromuscular disorder characterized by clinical features of a congenital myopathy and centrally placed nuclei on muscle biopsy.

nodes.name: frontotemporal dementia and/or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis 4
nodes.description: An amyotrophic lateral sclerosis that has material basis in mutation in the TBK1 gene on chromosome 12q14.

nodes.name: Proteus syndrome
nodes.description: Proteus syndrome (PS) is a very rare and complex hamartomatous overgrowth disorder characterized by progressive overgrowth of the skeleton, skin, adipose, and central nervous systems.

nodes.name: Cowden syndrome 6
nodes.description: Any Cowden disease in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the AKT1 gene.

nodes.name: PTEN hamartoma tumor syndrome
nodes.description: An autosomal dominant syndrome caused by pathogenic variants in the PTEN gene, characterized by hamartomas, overgrowth, neurodevelopmental disorders and an increased risk of various cancers, including breast, thyroid, and endometrial cancer. PHTS encompasses Cowden syndrome, Bannayan-Riley-Ruvalcaba syndrome, and Proteus-like syndrome.

nodes.name: bone Paget disease
nodes.description: A disease of bone that initially results in the excessive resorption of bone (by osteoclasts) followed by the replacement of normal bone marrow with vascular and fibrous tissue.

nodes.name: neurodegeneration with ataxia, dystonia, and gaze palsy, childhood-onset
behavioral variant of frontotemporal dementia
nodes.description: Behavioral variant of frontotemporal dementia (bv-FTD) is a form of frontotemporal dementia (FTD), characterized by progressive behavioral impairment and a decline in executive function with frontal lobe-predominant atrophy.

nodes.name: SQSTM1-related multisystem proteinopathy
nodes.description: A group of disorders including Paget disease of bone (PBD), inclusion body myopathy (IBM), and less frequently frontotemporal dementia (FTD) and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Phenotypic presentation and severity are highly variable, and individuals within the same family may present with different associated conditions.

nodes.name: frontotemporal dementia and/or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis 3
nodes.description: An amyotrophic lateral sclerosis that has material basis in mutation in the SQSTM1 gene on chromosome 5q35.

nodes.name: spastic tetraplegia and axial hypotonia, progressive
agenesis of the corpus callosum with peripheral neuropathy
nodes.description: Corpus callosum agenesis-neuropathy is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by severe progressive sensorimotor neuropathy beginning in infancy with resulting hypotonia, areflexia, amyotrophy and variable degrees of dysgenesis of the corpus callosum. Additional features include mild-to-severe intellectual and developmental delays, and psychiatric manifestations that include paranoid delusions

nodes.name: nephronophthisis 4
nodes.description: Any nephronophthisis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the NPHP4 gene.

nodes.name: Senior-Loken syndrome 4
nodes.description: Any Senior-Loken syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the NPHP4 gene.

nodes.name: syndromic X-linked intellectual disability Hedera type
nodes.description: X-linked intellectual disability, Hedera type is a rare X-linked intellectual disability syndrome characterized by an onset in infancy of delayed motor and speech milestones, generalized tonic-clonic seizures and drop attacks, and mild to moderate intellectual disability. nodes.name: X-linked parkinsonism-spasticity syndrome
nodes.description: X-linked parkinsonism-spasticity syndrome is a rare genetic neurological disorder characterized by parkinsonian features (including resting or action tremor, cogwheel rigidity, hypomimia and bradykinesia) associated with variably penetrant spasticity, hyperactive deep tendon reflexes and Babinski sign.

nodes.name: ATP6AP2-related disorder
nodes.description: Variants in the gene ATP6AP2 have been associated with a multitude of diseases, including X-linked syndromic ID Hedera type, X-linked Parkinsonism-spasticity syndrome, and congenital disorder of glycosylation type 2R. nodes.name: congenital disorder of glycosylation, type IIr
lethal multiple pterygium syndrome
nodes.description: Multiple pterygium syndrome lethal type is a very rare genetic condition affecting the skin, muscles and skeleton. It is characterized by minor facial abnormalities, prenatal growth deficiency, spine defects, joint contractures, and webbing (pterygia)of the neck, elbows, back of the knees, armpits, and fingers. Fetuses with this condition are usually not born. Some of the prenatal complications in

nodes.name: congenital myasthenic syndrome 3A
nodes.description: A congenital myasthenic syndrome characterized by autosomal dominant inheritance of postsynaptic neuromuscular junction defects resulting in prolonged synaptic currents and early-onset progressive muscle weakness that has material basis in heterozygous mutation in the CHRND gene on chromosome 2q37.

nodes.name: congenital myasthenic syndrome 3B
nodes.description: A congenital myasthenic syndrome characterized by autosomal recessive inheritance of postsynaptic neuromuscular junction defects resulting in rapid decay in endplate current and a failure to reach the threshold for depolarization and early onset progressive muscular weakness that has material basis in homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the CHRND gene on chromosome 2q37.

nodes.name: congenital myasthenic syndrome 3C
nodes.description: A congenital myasthenic syndrome characterized by autosomal recessive inheritance of postsynaptic neuromuscular junction defects, low amplitude of the miniature endplate potential and current, and early-onset muscle weakness that has material basis in compound heterozygous mutation in the CHRND gene on chromosome 2q37.

nodes.name: fetal akinesia deformation sequence
nodes.description: Fetal akinesia deformation sequence (FADS) is a condition characterized by decreased fetal movement (fetal akinesia) as well as intra-uterine growth restriction (IUGR), multiple joint contractures (arthrogryposis), facial anomalies, underdevelopment of the lungs (pulmonary hypoplasia) and other developmental abnormalities. nodes.name: congenital myasthenic syndrome 11
nodes.description: Any congenital myasthenic syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the RAPSN gene.

nodes.name: fetal akinesia deformation sequence 2
nodes.description: Any fetal akinesia deformation sequence in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the RAPSN gene.

nodes.name: congenital myasthenic syndrome 9
nodes.description: Any congenital myasthenic syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the MUSK gene.

nodes.name: congenital myasthenic syndrome 4

nodes.name: fetal akinesia deformation sequence 1
nodes.description: Any fetal akinesia deformation sequence in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the MUSK gene.

nodes.name: G6PD deficiency
nodes.description: An X-linked genetic condition caused by alterations in the gene G6PD that result in moderately to severely decreased activity levels of the enzyme glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase. nodes.name: FG syndrome 4
nodes.description: Any FG syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the CASK gene.

nodes.name: syndromic X-linked intellectual disability Najm type
nodes.description: A rare cerebellar dysgenesis syndrome characterized by variable clinical manifestations ranging from mild intellectual deficit with or without congenital nystagmus, to severe cognitive impairment associated with cerebellar and pontine hypoplasia/atrophy and abnormalities of cortical development.

nodes.name: inborn disorder of pentose phosphate metabolism
anemia due to erythrocyte enzyme disorder
nodes.description: Any form of anemia that results from the absence of, or the defective action of, any enzyme involved in erythropoiesis.

nodes.name: anemia, nonspherocytic hemolytic, due to G6PD deficiency

nodes.description: Pachyonychia congenita (PC) is a rare genodermatosis predominantly featuring painful palmoplantar keratoderma, thickened nails, cysts and whitish oral mucosa.

nodes.description: Isolated cryptophtalmia is a congenital abnormality in which the eyelids are absent and skin covers the ocular bulb, which is often microphthalmic. Six cases of complete bilateral crytophthalmia have been described. Transmission is autosomal dominant.

nodes.name: Fraser syndrome
nodes.description: Fraser syndrome is a rare clinical entity including as main characteristics cryptophthalmos and syndactyly.

nodes.name: syndromic microphthalmia
nodes.description: A microphthalmia that is part of a larger syndrome.

nodes.name: nephrocalcinosis
nodes.description: Nephrocalcinosis is a disorder that occurs when too much calcium is deposited in the kidneys. It commonly occurs in premature infants. Individuals may not have symptoms or may have symptoms related to thecondition causing nephrocalcinosis. nodes.name: renal tubular transport disease
nodes.description: Genetic defects in the selective or non-selective transport functions of the kidney tubules.

nodes.name: familial primary hypomagnesemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis
nodes.description: Familial primary hypomagnesemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis (FHHNC) is a form of familial primary hypomagnesemia (FPH), characterized by renal magnesium (Mg) and calcium (Ca) wasting, nephrocalcinosis, kidney failure and, in some cases, severe ocular impairment. Two subtypes of FHHNC are described: FHHNC with severe ocular involvement (FHHNCOI) and without severe ocular involvement (F

nodes.name: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease axonal type 2N
nodes.description: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2N (CMT2N) is a mild form of axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, a peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy, characterized by distal legs sensory loss and weakness that can be asymmetric. Tendon reflexes are reduced in the knees and absent in ankles. Progression is slow.

nodes.name: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 29
nodes.description: Any early infantile epileptic encephalopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the AARS gene.

nodes.name: trichothiodystrophy
nodes.description: Trichothiodystrophy or TTD is a heterogeneous group disorders characterized by short, brittle hair with low-sulphur content (due to an abnormal synthesis of the sulfur containing keratins).

nodes.name: AARS1-related leukoencephalopathy
nodes.description: Any leukoencephalopathy in which the cause of the disease is a variant in the AARS1 gene.

nodes.name: hereditary nephritis
nodes.description: A group of inherited conditions characterized initially by hematuria and slowly progressing to renal insufficiency. The most common form is the Alport syndrome (hereditary nephritis with hearing loss) which is caused by mutations in genes for type IV collagen and defective glomerular basement membrane.

nodes.name: primary membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis
nodes.description: A rare glomerular disease characterized by a pattern of glomerular injury on kidney biopsy with characteristic light microscopic changes: mesangial hypercellularity, endocapillary proliferation, and thickening of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM). nodes.name: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease axonal type 2S
nodes.description: Any Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the IGHMBP2 gene.

nodes.name: autosomal recessive distal spinal muscular atrophy 1
nodes.description: Spinal muscular atrophy with respiratory distress type 1 is a rare genetic motor neuron disease characterized by severe respiratory distress/respiratory failure in association with diaphragmatic eventration and palsy, as well as progressive, symmetrical, distal-to-proximal muscle weakness and atrophy (in lower limbs especially). Patients typically have a history of intrauterine growth retardation,

nodes.name: congenital bilateral aplasia of vas deferens from CFTR mutation
nodes.description: An autosomal recessive disorder that is associated with mutation(s) in the CFTR gene, encoding cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator. Mutation(s) in the same gene are associated with cystic fibrosis.

nodes.name: congenital bilateral absence of vas deferens
nodes.description: Congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens (CBAVD) is a condition leading to male infertility.

nodes.name: CFTR-related disorder
nodes.description: A disease associated with CFTR (cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator) dysfunction that does not fulfill the diagnostic criteria for cystic fibrosis (CF). nodes.name: cystic fibrosis

nodes.name: ataxia-pancytopenia syndrome
nodes.description: A rare genetic disease characterized by cerebellar ataxia, cytopenias and predisposition to bone marrow failure and myeloid leukemia. nodes.name: autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia
nodes.description: A clinically and genetically heterogeneous group of neurodegenerative diseases characterized by a slowly progressive ataxia of gait, stance and limbs, dysarthria and/or oculomotor disorder, due to cerebellar degeneration in the absence of coexisting diseases. nodes.name: hereditary cerebellar ataxia
nodes.description: Cerebellar ataxia that is transmitted from parent to child.

nodes.name: autosomal dominant nonsyndromic hearing loss 67
nodes.description: Any autosomal dominant nonsyndromic deafness in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the OSBPL2 gene.

nodes.name: dyschromatosis, ichthyosis, deafness, and atopic disease
Aicardi-Goutieres syndrome 6

nodes.description: Any type 1 interferonopathies in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the ADAR gene. Individuals with variants in ADAR can present with a variety of phenotypes, including Aicardi-Goutieres syndrome and dyschromatosis symmetrica hereditaria.

nodes.name: dyschromatosis symmetrica hereditaria
nodes.description: Acropigmentation of Dohi is a genodermatosis characterized by the presence of hyperpigmented and hypopigmented macules, principally located on the extremities and limbs.

nodes.name: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 31A
nodes.description: Any developmental and epileptic encephalopathy in which the cause of the disease is a heterozygous mutation in the DNM1 gene.

nodes.name: developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 31B
nodes.description: Any developmental and epileptic encephalopathy in which the cause of the disease is a homozygous mutation in the DNM1 gene.

nodes.name: Lennox-Gastaut syndrome
nodes.description: Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (LGS) belongs to the group of severe childhood epileptic encephalopathies.

nodes.name: DNM1-encephalopathy and neurodevelopmental disorder
nodes.description: A developmental and epileptic encephalopathy in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the DNM1 gene.

nodes.name: mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome 3 (hepatocerebral type)
nodes.description: Any mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the DGUOK gene.

nodes.description: An extremely rare multiple mitochondrial DNA deletion syndrome with markedly decreased deoxyguanosine kinase (DGUOK) activity in skeletal muscle characterized by a highly variable phenotype. nodes.name: familial hyperaldosteronism type II
nodes.description: Familial hyperaldosteronism type II (FH-II) is a heritable form of primary aldosteronism (PA) characterized by hypertension of varying severity, and non glucocticoid remediable hyperaldosteronism.

nodes.name: leukoencephalopathy with mild cerebellar ataxia and white matter edema
familial hyperaldosteronism

nodes.name: adrenal cortex neoplasm
nodes.description: A benign or malignant (primary or metastatic) neoplasm affecting the adrenal cortex. (NCI05)

nodes.name: homocystinuria
nodes.description: An autosomal recessive inherited metabolic disorder caused by mutations in the CBS, MTHFR, MTR, and MTRR genes. It may affect the cardiovascular, musculoskeletal and the central nervous systems.

nodes.name: disorder of folate metabolism and transport
Acromicric dysplasia
nodes.description: A rare bone dysplasia characterized by short stature, short hands and feet, mild facial dysmorphism, and characteristic X-ray abnormalities of the hands.

nodes.name: ectopia lentis 1, isolated, autosomal dominant
nodes.description: Any isolated ectopia lentis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the FBN1 gene.

nodes.name: Marfan syndrome
nodes.description: A disorder of the connective tissue. Connective tissue provides strength and flexibility to structures throughout the body such as bones, ligaments, muscles, walls of blood vessels, and heart valves. Marfan syndrome affects most organs and tissues, especially the skeleton, lungs, eyes, heart, and the large blood vessel that distributes blood from the heart to the rest of the body (the aorta). nodes.name: stiff skin syndrome
nodes.description: A rare syndrome characterized by hard, thick skin, usually on the entire body. The thickening of the skin can limit joint mobility and causes joints to be stuck in a bent position (flexion contractures). nodes.name: MASS syndrome
nodes.description: A genetic disorder of connective tissue caused by mutations in the FBN1 gene. Connective tissue is the material between the cells of the body that gives tissues form and strength. nodes.name: Weill-Marchesani syndrome 2, dominant
nodes.description: A Weill-Marchesani syndrome characterized by progressive joint stiffness, glaucoma, short stature and lens dislocation. It has been described in three members of a family (the grandfather, his daughter and grandson). It is likely to be transmitted as an autosomal dominant trait. nodes.name: geleophysic dysplasia 2
nodes.description: Any geleophysic dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the FBN1 gene.

nodes.name: dyskeratosis congenita, autosomal recessive 6
nodes.description: Any dyskeratosis congenita in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the PARN gene.

nodes.name: pulmonary fibrosis and/or bone marrow failure, Telomere-related, 4
nodes.description: Any pulmonary fibrosis and/or bone marrow failure, Telomere-related in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the PARN gene.

nodes.name: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease axonal type 2Q
nodes.description: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2Q is a rare subtype of autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 characterized by adolescent to adulthood-onset of symmetrical, slowly progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy (with a predominant weakness of the distal lower limbs) associated with reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes, pes cavus and mild to moderated deep sens

nutritional deficiency disease
nodes.description: A condition produced by dietary or metabolic deficiency. The term includes all diseases caused by an insufficient supply of essential nutrients, i.e., protein (or amino acids), vitamins, and minerals. It also includes an inadequacy of calories. (From Dorland, 27th ed; Stedman, 25th ed)

nodes.name: stapes ankylosis with broad thumbs and toes
nodes.description: Stapes ankylosis with broad thumbs and toes is a very rare genetic bone disorder characterized by ankylosis of stapes, broad thumbs and halluces, conductive hearing loss and hyperopia.

nodes.name: multiple synostoses syndrome 1
nodes.description: Any multiple synostoses syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the NOG gene.

nodes.name: tarsal-carpal coalition syndrome
nodes.description: Tarsal-carpal coalition syndrome is characterized by fusion of the carpals, tarsals, and phalanges.

nodes.name: brachydactyly type B2
nodes.description: Brachydactyly type B2 is a rare, genetic congenital limb malformation disorder characterized by hypoplasia/aplasia of distal and/or middle phalanges in fingers and toes II-V (frequently severe in fingers/toes IV-V, milder in fingers/toes II-III) in association with proximal, and occasionally distal, symphalangism, fusion of carpal/tarsal bones and partial cutaneous syndactyly. nodes.name: NOG-related symphalangism spectrum disorder
nodes.description: An autosomal dominant condition caused by pathogenic variants of the NOG gene, encoding the noggin protein. nodes.name: oculocutaneous albinism type 1
nodes.description: Type 1 oculocutaneous albinism (OCA1) describes a group of tyrosine related OCAs that includes OCA1A, OCA1B, type 1 minimal pigment oculocutaneous albinism (OCA1-MP) and type 1 temperature sensitive oculocutaneous albinism (OCA1-TS).

nodes.name: autosomal recessive ocular albinism
nodes.description: Autosomal recessive form of ocular albinism (disease).

nodes.name: coagulation protein disease
nodes.description: Congenital or acquired deficiency of one of the coagulation factors. It results in bleeding.

nodes.name: hemorrhagic disease
nodes.description: Spontaneous or near spontaneous bleeding caused by a defect in clotting mechanisms (blood coagulation disorders) or another abnormality causing a structural flaw in the blood vessels (hemostatic disorders).

nodes.name: inherited thrombophilia
nodes.description: An instance of thrombophilia that is inherited.

nodes.name: thrombophilia due to activated protein C resistance
nodes.description: A hemostatic disorder characterized by a poor anticoagulant response to activated protein C (APC). The activated form of Factor V (Factor Va) is more slowly degraded by activated protein C. Factor V Leiden mutation (R506Q) is the most common cause of APC resistance.

nodes.name: factor V deficiency
nodes.description: A coagulation disorder characterized by the partial or complete absence of factor V activity in the blood.

nodes.name: congenital factor V deficiency
nodes.description: Congenital factor V deficiency is an inherited bleeding disorder due to reduced plasma levels of factor V (FV) and characterized by mild to severe bleeding symptoms.

nodes.name: autosomal recessive spinocerebellar ataxia 13

nodes.name: autosomal recessive cerebellar ataxia - pyramidal signs - nystagmus - oculomotor apraxia syndrome
nodes.description: Autosomal recessive cerebellar ataxia-pyramidal signs-nystagmus-oculomotor apraxia syndrome is a rare, genetic, slowly progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by delayed psychomotor development beginning in infancy, mild to profound intellectual disability, gait and stance ataxia, pyramidal signs (hyperreflexia, extensor plantar responses), dysarthria, and ocular abnormalities (e.g. ny

nodes.name: combined oxidative phosphorylation defect type 7
nodes.description: Combined oxidative phosphorylation defect type 7 is a rare mitochondrial disease due to a defect in mitochondrial protein synthesis characterized by a variable phenotype that includes onset in infancy or early childhood of failure to thrive and psychomotor regression (after initial normal development), as well as ocular manifestations (such as ptosis, nystagmus, optic atrophy, ophthalmoplegia and

nodes.name: thrombophilia due to thrombin defect
nodes.description: The formation of a blood clot (thrombus) in the lumen of a vein.

nodes.name: congenital vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors deficiency
nodes.description: Congenital vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors deficiency involving multiple coagulation factors.

nodes.name: congenital prothrombin deficiency
nodes.description: Congenital factor II deficiency is an inherited bleeding disorder due to reduced activity of factor II (FII, prothrombin) and characterized by mucocutaneous bleeding symptoms.

nodes.name: mandibulofacial dysostosis
nodes.description: A hereditary disorder occurring in two forms: the complete form (Franceschetti's syndrome) is characterized by antimongoloid slant of the palpebral fissures, coloboma of the lower lid, micrognathia and hypoplasia of the zygomatic arches, and microtia. nodes.name: congenital myopathy 2a, typical, autosomal dominant
nodes.description: An inherited myopathy caused by mutations in the ACTA1 gene, encoding actin, alpha skeletal muscle. The phenotype is highly variable, and as such attempts at classification by clinical features is not optimal. Generally, affected individuals have generalized muscle weakness, typically involving proximal muscles, the face, bulbar and respiratory muscles.

nodes.name: severe congenital nemaline myopathy
nodes.description: Severe congenital nemaline myopathy is a severe form of nemaline myopathy (NM) characterized by severe hypotonia with little spontaneous movement in neonates.

nodes.name: rigid spine syndrome

nodes.name: alpha-actinopathy
nodes.description: A musculoskeletal system disorder that covers a wide spectrum of phenotypes and is caused by pathogenic variants in the skeletal muscle α-actin gene (ACTA1). nodes.name: hereditary spastic paraplegia 43
nodes.description: Autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia type 43 is a rare, complex hereditary spastic paraplegia characterized by a childhood to adolescent onset of progressive lower limb spasticity, associated with mild to severe gait disturbances, extensor plantar responses, muscle weakness and severe distal atrophy, frequently with upper limb involvement. nodes.name: neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation
nodes.description: Neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation (NBIA, formerly Hallervorden-Spatz syndrome) encompasses a group of rare neurodegenerative disorders characterized by progressive extrapyramidal dysfunction (dystonia, rigidity, choreoathetosis), iron accumulation in the brain and the presence of axonal spheroids, usually limited to the central nervous system.

autosomal dominant mitochondrial myopathy with exercise intolerance
proximal spinal muscular atrophy
nodes.description: Proximal spinal muscular atrophies are a group of neuromuscular disorders characterized by progressive muscle weakness resulting from the degeneration and loss of the lower motor neurons in the spinal cord and the brain stem nuclei.

nodes.name: frontotemporal dementia and/or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis 2
nodes.description: An amyotrophic lateral sclerosis that has material basis in mutation in the CHCHD10 gene on chromosome 22. It is characterized by adult onset of either frontotemporal dementia and/or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.

nodes.name: amyotrophic lateral sclerosis type 2, juvenile
nodes.description: Any amyotrophic lateral sclerosis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ALS2 gene.

nodes.name: juvenile primary lateral sclerosis
nodes.description: Juvenile primary lateral sclerosis (JPLS) is a very rare motor neuron disease characterized by progressive upper motor neuron dysfunction leading to loss of the ability to walk with wheelchair dependence, and subsequently, loss of motor speech production.

nodes.name: infantile-onset ascending hereditary spastic paralysis
nodes.description: Infantile-onset ascending hereditary spastic paralysis (IAHSP) is a very rare motor neuron disease characterized by severe spasticity of the lower limbs in early life, progression of spasticity to the upper limbs in late childhood, and dysarthria.

nodes.name: lateral sclerosis
nodes.description: Primary lateral sclerosis (PLS) is an idiopathic non-familial motor neuron disease characterized by slowly progressive upper motor neuron dysfunction leading to spasticity, mild weakness in voluntary muscle movement, hyperreflexia, and loss of motor speech production.

nodes.name: ALS2-related motor neuron disease
nodes.description: Any motor neuron disease in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ALS2 gene.

nodes.name: LRIT3-related retinopathy
nodes.description: Any retinopathy caused by variants in the LRIT3 gene.

nodes.name: hypotrichosis simplex
nodes.description: Hypotrichosis simplex (HS) or hereditary hypotrichosis simplex (HHS) is characterized by reduced pilosity over the scalp and body (with sparse, thin, and short hair) in the absence of other anomalies.

nodes.name: focal segmental glomerulosclerosis 9
nodes.description: Any focal segmental glomerulosclerosis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the CRB2 gene.

nodes.name: Bothnia retinal dystrophy
nodes.description: A rare form of retinal dystrophy, seen mostly in Northern Sweden, presenting in early childhood with night blindness and progressive maculopathy with a decrease in visual acuity, eventually leading to blindness by adulthood. nodes.name: Newfoundland cone-rod dystrophy
nodes.description: Any cone-rod dystrophy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the RLBP1 gene.

nodes.name: photosensitive trichothiodystrophy

nodes.name: xeroderma pigmentosum group B
nodes.description: Any xeroderma pigmentosum in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ERCC3 gene.

nodes.name: short-rib thoracic dysplasia 10 with or without polydactyly

nodes.name: retinitis pigmentosa 71
nodes.description: Any retinitis pigmentosa in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the IFT172 gene.

nodes.description: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 19 (SCA19) is a very rare subtype of type I autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia (ADCA type I). nodes.description: A malignant, invasive embryonal neoplasm arising from the cerebellum. It occurs predominantly in children and has the tendency to metastasize via the cerebrospinal fluid pathways. nodes.name: severe intellectual disability-progressive spastic diplegia syndrome
nodes.description: Severe intellectual disability-progressive spastic diplegia syndrome is a rare condition that has been described in a few people with severe intellectual disability. nodes.description: Any neurodevelopmental disorder and/or exudative vitreoretinopathy caused by a monoallelic variant in the CTNNB1 gene. nodes.name: multifocal dystonia

nodes.name: hypomaturation-hypoplastic amelogenesis imperfecta with taurodontism

nodes.description: Amelogenesis imperfecta (AI) represents a group of developmental conditions affecting the structure and clinical appearance of the enamel of all or nearly all the teeth in a more or less equal manner, and which may be associated with morphologic or biochemical changes elsewhere in the body.

nodes.name: Temple-Baraitser syndrome
